- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.33) or shows strong downward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >85) — model tends to overreact and peak too high.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model often fails to correct after 3–5 consecutive high forecasts.
- Lag in downward corrections: model delays price drop recognition when sentiment turns negative.
- Overweight recent history in forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), leading to overfitting.
- Avoid extrapolating upward trends beyond 3–4 consecutive high sentiment days without validation.
- Adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment turns negative and price has been rising for 5+ days.
- Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is low or mixed — model tends to overestimate uncertainty.
